title: Spectral spacing grid and asymmetric radius presets for interactive rows
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Create a cohesive token subset that balances dense data surfaces (tables, chart panels) with interactive touch targets (buttons, row actions) by introducing a spectral spacing grid and asymmetric radius presets, plus a gentle elevation microcurve for perceived depth across density modes. This ticket covers research, token definitions, component mapping, Figma assets, and a migration plan for the component library.
background: We get repeated requests to support both compact analytics views (dense tables and sparkline-heavy cards) and touch-first action surfaces (primary/secondary buttons in mobile/responsive). Current token set treats radius and spacing symmetrically, which leads to cramped touch targets or visually floating dense rows. Shadow ramps are linear and produce either flat or overly pronounced depth when scaled. We need a token approach that: 1) preserves accessibility contrast and hit area, 2) reduces token churn for engineers, 3) supports theming (light/dark) and density toggles.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Define a spectral spacing grid (6-step variable) and publish tokens: spacing.s-1 .. spacing.s-6 with explicit px and rem values. 2) Define asymmetric radius presets for interactive rows and buttons (radius.touch-leading, radius.touch-trailing, radius.data-row) with guidance for left/right language adaptivity. 3) Introduce elevation.microcurve tokens (elev.micro-0..3) with CSS shadow tokens for light/dark that pass visual contrast checks. 4) Provide Figma component variants for Button (primary/secondary/ghost), TableRow (compact / normal / touch-friendly), and ChartCard (compact / regular) wired to tokens. 5) Publish migration guide and a single PR that updates token import and two example components in the component library. 6) Run accessibility checklists and get final PM approval.
design_decisions: - Use an asymmetric radius approach: leading edge larger to accommodate touch reach on mobile; trailing edge smaller to avoid crowding adjacent cells. - Spectral spacing grid emphasizes multiples of 4 and 6 to align with typography line-heights and chart gutters. - Elevation microcurve is non-linear: small increments at low elevations and slightly larger at higher steps to mimic physical penumbra. - Keep token names semantic and density-agnostic so devs can choose density presets instead of swapping tokens for every component.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Asymmetric radius introduces complexity in legacy components; will need narrow migration adapters. - Changing spacing may shift layouts in dashboards—requires visual QA and minor layout tweaks. - Slight visual difference across themes may need per-theme tweaks of shadow color/alpha; avoid per-component overrides unless necessary.
implementation_notes: - Primary deliverable: tokens JSON + CSS variable mapping + Figma library page. - Work with frontend eng to provide a compatibility shim that maps old tokens to new ones for initial rollout. - Add unit tests that assert CSS variables exist and snapshot key components for compact/regular densities. - Coordinate with runtime team for console rollout to ensure instrumentation (token usage telemetry) is preserved.
qa_and_rollout_plan: 1) Merge token JSON and compatibility shim behind feature flag. 2) Deploy to staging and verify dashboard widgets and default pages. 3) Run visual diff (Chromatic) for Button, TableRow, ChartCard in both compact and regular densities. 4) If diffs exceed threshold, revert and iterate. 5) After sign-off, flip feature flag and monitor user-facing telemetry for layout regressions.
